title: Paying when heat strikes: heat risk finance in South and Southeast Asia
disclaimer: Listing is not endorsement and is not financial, insurance or investment advice.
rules: Money is kept in its kind: premiums, cover limits, payouts and budgets are never added together.
Warning, action and payout triggers are kept apart.
Every scheme records whether it paid, and when; 'never triggered' is a valid finding.
Known, inferred and uncertain are kept distinct.
Links that failed our link check are left out.

layers.name: Through systems that already reach people
layers.text: Cash transfers, employment guarantees, health cover and bill relief that pay more, or earlier, in a heatwave.

layers.name: Money kept ready
layers.text: Budgets, reserves and disaster funds that a government, city or organisation keeps for the heat it expects most years.

layers.name: Money released on a forecast
layers.text: Funds agreed in advance and released when a forecast crosses a threshold, so help arrives before the worst heat.

layers.name: Credit and budgets arranged in advance
layers.text: Credit lines and budget reallocations that can be drawn quickly when a declared or measured event exceeds what was kept.

layers.name: Risk shared with insurers and markets
layers.text: Insurance, regional pools and catastrophe bonds that pay when a contracted trigger is met, usually for rarer, more severe years.

instruments.def: Public spending authority is agreed before a shock so funds can be redirected or released under specified rules.

instruments.def: Cash or legally earmarked resources are held for eligible disaster spending; dedicated heat funds require explicit rules.

instruments.def: A forecast meeting agreed conditions releases pre-arranged resources for specified early actions.

instruments.def: An existing benefit system increases payments or temporarily adds eligible people after a pre-agreed shock.

instruments.limits: Contributory employment rules may exclude informal and unregistered workers.
instruments.basis: Eligibility and recognition of a work stoppage can miss actual harm.
instruments.poorestWhy: Formal-sector protection is verified in ILO guidance; informal inclusion not verified.
